answer: In an AI agent economy, Sybil resistance can be achieved by requiring each agent to bond a unique non-fungible credential derived from a scarce historical relic, such as a verified onyx-embedded pearl token that is expensive to fabricate in bulk. Attackers attempting to create multiple identities face escalating costs because each fake agent must acquire and lock a distinct relic-derived proof, whose scarcity and verification overhead make large-scale identity farming economically unviable while honest agents reuse a single validated credential across sessions.
